page.layout: One page of text, running head at top centre; verse block of eight lines in the upper part; signature-like mark "E 3" to the right below the verse; a woodcut ornament (roundel of scrollwork) in the lower middle. No margin notes.

main_text.p:
Nunc tandem iunctâ foedere Pierides,
Vana Vetustatis fallat Vos abfit imago,
Quae Tenebras Vobis suadeat esse Diem,
Vestrum immo retinete decus, purumque nitore,
Quo radiat toto pulchrius orbe nihil,
Hoc Superum concede Pater, si Vera poësis
Muneris haud falsò creditur esse tui.
Barbaries Musis quum cesserit ipsa renatis,
Abfit Vt has possit ladere Scabrities.

page.notes: The verse is set in italic type; the first line begins with a raised quotation-like mark. Some letters in the verse (such as the initial V's written as Vo, Ve) are printed as in the original, and the line "Quae Tenebras" uses a long-s form read as Vobis. Lines 4 and 9 show damage near the ink stain; "retinete" and "ladere" are read with some uncertainty. The woodcut ornament is not transcribed as text. The signature "E 3" stands at the right, apart from the verse.
